The *Samuddaṅgapañha* ("The Sea", Mil 7.3.10) is a dialogue in the *Milindapañha* that examines the spiritual qualities to be adopted by a practitioner through the simile or attributes (*aṅga*) of the ocean (*samudda*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral lists three translations of the text across three modern languages [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral notes thematic links or mentions between this text and canonical accounts of the ocean's remarkable qualities, including the *Pahārādasutta* (AN 8.19), the *Uposathasutta* (AN 8.20; Ud 5.5), the Vinaya *Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhaka* (Kd 19), two *Kathāvatthu* debates (Kv 2.9, Kv 12.8), and the *Mahāsutasomajātaka* (Ja 537) [SuttaCentral].
